title: Vishal Mega Mart Shares Tumble After Q1 Results Despite 26% Profit Jump
excerpt: India's largest value retail chain reported ₹258.8 crore in net profit and ₹3,727 crore in revenue for the June 2026 quarter, but decelerating growth and leadership changes weighed on investor sentiment.
body:
• Consolidated net profit rose 25.6% YoY to ₹258.8 crore; revenue increased 18.7% to ₹3,727 crore in Q1 FY27.
  • Same-store sales grew 10% with gross margins holding steady; 27 new stores added during the quarter.
  • Stock fell as much as 5% intraday as profit growth decelerated from 37% in Q1 FY26, raising questions about momentum.
  • Promoter Kedaara Capital continued reducing its stake to 40%, while COO Manoj Kumar’s resignation added to investor concerns.

Strong Quarter, Weak Reception

Vishal Mega Mart’s shares dropped as much as 5% on Wednesday after the company reported its first-quarter results for fiscal year 2027, even as the value retailer posted double-digit growth across all key financial metrics.

The company’s consolidated net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, rose 25.6% year-on-year to ₹258.8 crore, up from ₹206 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations climbed 18.7% to ₹3,727 crore, compared with ₹3,140 crore in Q1 FY26, according to a regulatory filing with the Bombay Stock Exchange.

Same-store sales growth came in at 10%, and gross margins held steady during the quarter, the company said. Vishal Mega Mart added 27 new stores during the period, expanding its network to approximately 822 outlets across India.

Why Investors Sold Despite Solid Profit Growth

The sell-off, which pushed shares to an intraday low of ₹106.31 before a partial recovery to around ₹110, reflects investor discomfort with the pace of growth deceleration rather than the absolute numbers.

In Q1 FY26, Vishal Mega Mart had reported a 37.2% surge in net profit and 21% revenue growth — both significantly faster than the latest quarter’s performance. Revenue growth slowed from 21% to 18.7%, while profit growth nearly halved from 37% to 26%.

“Growth was mainly driven by continued strength of our own brands portfolio, strong footfall and store additions.”

— Gunender Kapur, MD & CEO, Vishal Mega Mart

The deceleration comes as India’s retail sector faces mixed consumer spending signals. While rural demand has shown signs of recovery, urban consumption growth has remained tepid, with discretionary spending under pressure from persistent food inflation and elevated housing costs.

Leadership Shakeup and Promoter Exit

Adding to investor unease, Vishal Mega Mart’s Chief Operating Officer Manoj Kumar resigned on July 16, 2026, with his last working day set for September 11. The company has not yet announced a replacement, creating uncertainty around operational leadership during a critical expansion phase.

The shareholding pattern reveals a dramatic ongoing exit by promoter entity Kedaara Capital. The promoter’s stake has declined from 76% in December 2024 to just 40.09% as of June 2026. Kedaara, a private equity firm that backed the Vishal Mega Mart acquisition in 2018, has been steadily monetizing its investment since the company’s December 2024 IPO. In June 2025, it sold a 10% stake through a block deal at ₹110 per share.

The board on Wednesday also proposed setting a 49.99% cap on foreign ownership, a move that could limit the pool of international institutional investors in the stock. Foreign institutional investors currently hold approximately 20.4% of the company.

Valuation Leaves Little Room for Disappointment

Vishal Mega Mart’s stock has been under sustained pressure, falling 23% from its 52-week high of ₹157.60. At around ₹110, the stock trades at roughly 61 times trailing twelve-month consolidated earnings — a premium that demands consistent high growth to justify.

For context, the company delivered strong results in fiscal year 2026: consolidated revenue of ₹12,906 crore with net profit of ₹839 crore, posting growth of 20% and 33% respectively. As of March 2026, the retailer operated 795 stores across 535 cities in 30 states and union territories, with a retail footprint of 13.45 million square feet.

What’s Next

The Q1 FY27 earnings conference call, scheduled for 4:00 PM IST on Wednesday, will be closely watched for management commentary on the margin outlook, impact of the COO departure, and store expansion targets for the remainder of fiscal 2027.

Analysts had previously forecast consolidated revenue growth of about 19% and net profit growth of around 22% for FY27 — estimates that the Q1 results broadly track. Whether the market’s sharp reaction reflects a temporary reassessment or a more lasting rerating will depend on whether same-store sales momentum and margin stability hold through the seasonally stronger second half of the year.

For Indian diaspora investors who have tracked the stock since its December 2024 IPO, the Q1 results underscore a familiar tension: strong retail fundamentals that struggle to justify elevated valuations when growth begins to normalize.
